title: Credit Policy on Overadvances for Operating Lines of Credit
content:
Only an Operating Lines of Credit product with an overadvance tolerance above zero may book an advance larger than the line's available credit.

## Policy in force

1. **When an overadvance may be booked.** Only a product with an overadvance tolerance above zero may book an advance larger than the available credit computed under the conditions of advance, and only when the excess — the overadvance portion — is no larger than the product's overadvance tolerance percentage of the commitment in force, and no earlier overadvance on the line remains uncured.
2. **Cure.** An overadvance is cured when outstanding principal is back at or below the available credit.
3. **Cure period.** An overadvance must be cured within the product's overadvance cure period in calendar days after the effective date of the advance that created it, the effective date itself being day 0. If it is not cured by the end of the last day, advances are frozen for an uncured overadvance.
4. **Everywhere else.** On every other product, and above the tolerance on these, the advance is declined in full and no fee arises.

The tolerance amount is the commitment in force multiplied by the tolerance percentage, rounded to cents; an overadvance portion equal to that amount is within the tolerance.

## Clause no longer in force

- "The advance is booked in full and an overadvance fee equal to the product's overadvance fee rate of the overadvance portion, rounded to cents, is assessed the same day as a separate fee charge with the overadvance fee code whose source is that advance." — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis for the overadvance fee.

## Cases (hypothetical Borrowing Base Operating Line, commitment USD 2,000,000, tolerance 5%, so USD 100,000)

| Available credit before the advance | Advance asked | Overadvance portion | Earlier overadvance uncured | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| USD 50,000 | USD 120,000 | USD 70,000 | No | May be booked as an overadvance |
| USD 50,000 | USD 150,000 | USD 100,000 (equal to the tolerance) | No | May be booked as an overadvance |
| USD 50,000 | USD 160,000 | USD 110,000 | No | Declined in full, no fee |
| USD 50,000 | USD 120,000 | USD 70,000 | Yes | Declined in full, no fee |

## Cure period example (hypothetical dates)

With a 30-day cure period, an overadvance created by an advance effective 1 June must be cured by the end of 1 July (day 30). If principal is still above the available credit at the end of 1 July, advances are frozen.

superseded_clauses: The advance is booked in full and an overadvance fee equal to overadvance_fee_pct of the overadvance portion, rounded to cents, is assessed the same day as a separate fee row with fee_code overadvance whose source_txn_id is that advance.
